nodes.label: Patient presented with right-sided chest pain and dyspnoea for 1 month

Patient was a 66-year-old male, never-smoker, labourer; past history included right-sided pleural effusion 3 years ago treated for 6 months and blunt chest trauma 5 years ago from buffalo impact; no comorbidities, recent instrumentation or surgery.

Chest pain was dull aching, gradually progressive, increased with respiration, and relieved with analgesics; dyspnoea was exertional and gradual in onset, progressively increasing from mMRC grade 1 to 3; no fever, cough, expectoration, or wheeze.

Physical examination: pulse rate 96/min, respiratory rate 25/min, blood pressure 124/76 mmHg, oxygen saturation 96% on room air; respiratory system showed decreased movements in right mammary, infra-axillary, and infrascapular areas, dull percussion note, and decreased breath sounds in affected areas.
Pleural fluid is exudative with markedly elevated LDH and ADA
CT chest with contrast shows right-sided thickened pleura and hydropneumothorax with intercostal tube in situ
Pleural fluid cytology and biopsy pathology have not been performed
Patient has no known asbestos exposure history
